A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical definitions, constructions and proofs, including Appendices A–B. Its conceptual comparison table and references to empirical literature do not constitute original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 likewise reports theoretical constructions and proofs, including Appendices A–F. Empirical observations mentioned in its discussion are attributed to other works.

M1.justification: The principal SVM-to-HEA construction and tensor-product/counter-register recipe are retained; Theorem 8 and Corollary 9 become Theorem 3 and Corollary 4. v2 removes the auxiliary single-rotation kernel construction and separate gradient-trained LCU kernel variant from v1's Corollaries 6–7, narrowing the repertoire without redesigning the main models.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios in an empirical evaluation. DLP classification and hard-function learning tasks are theoretical constructions; v2's additional discussion of unsupervised learning and Hamiltonians introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. DLP kernels, HEA and other cited models serve as theoretical examples or related work.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Sampling assumptions, optimization objectives and Algorithm 1 describe the theoretical framework rather than conducted experiments.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or empirical case studies. The expanded appendix discussions concern definitions and theoretical model properties.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical tests. Their variance and concentration formulas are theoretical definitions.

E6.justification: Neither version contains numerical performance results or original empirical qualitative findings. Changes to mathematical results and model classifications are addressed under T1 and C2.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's training-set-dependent kernel-family treatment with the full family of linear functions of the feature map and revises the reasoning about gradient trainability (Appendices B.1 and E). Definition 2 retains only the distribution-averaged barren-plateau criterion, dropping the separate supremum formulation. Section 4.1 adds gradient trainability as a defining requirement of vari veryational models. v1's Proposition 2 proof and Corollaries 6–7 constructions disappear, while the principal existence theorem and counter-register proof remain.

C1.justification: The central claim that gradient-trainable, non-dequantizable variational QML models exist is retained. v2 focuses the contribution on the general recipe and vari veryational construction, dropping v1's explicit intermediate constructions across degrees of variationalness. Practical usefulness remains unestablished.

C2.justification: v1 treats kernel coefficient optimization as gradient-based training; v2 explains that restricting optimization to a data-dependent span prevents the complete procedure from qualifying under its stricter definition (Appendix E). v2 also adds limitations on certifying trainability in practice, expands the interpretation of vanishing similarity as a generalization problem, and discusses possible Hamiltonian/noise applications while retaining the contrived-construction caveat.

D1.justification: Removing v1's Corollary 7 also removes its explicit zero/Gaussian coefficient initialization and L1-normalization prescriptions. The retained Algorithm 1 and counter-register implementation details remain substantially unchanged, although relocated. Neither version supplies implementation code or experimental resource information.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work, v2 adds substantive comparisons with meta-learning, unsupervised distribution learning, and encoding-first, re-uploading and flipped QML models. It adds supporting works including Huang et al. (2021), Nietner (2023) and Barthe and Pérez-Salinas (2023), while pruning much of v1's broader citation coverage. The dequantization-without-simulation discussion replaces v1's explicit Proposition 2 proof with direct treatment as prior work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten. v1's extended definitions-and-discussion section is redistributed among concise definitions, a dedicated related-work section and thematic appendices. v2 adds quantum-computing background, relocates gradient-training exposition, and separates discussion from conclusion.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column preprint layout to a single-column conference layout. Figure 2 removes the intermediate somewhat-variational constructions, Figure 3 is substantially rearranged with revised relationship annotations, and Table I is removed. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix E, and Figure 1 is resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves conceptual precision by distinguishing the full kernel hypothesis family from its training-set span and explaining the end-to-end gradient-training requirement. Its reorganized exposition and explicit limitations make the retained main result easier to assess. The gain is limited: subsidiary constructions and a self-contained counterexample proof are removed, and Figure 3 still presents a kernel example under gradient-based trainability without reconciling it with Appendix E's stricter treatment.
